subsystems.name: Particle sensor
subsystems.role: counts and sizes airborne particles, giving PM1, PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations.

subsystems.name: Gas sensors
subsystems.role: measure carbon dioxide and total volatile organic compounds.

subsystems.name: Climate sensors
subsystems.role: measure temperature and relative humidity, which affect comfort, mould risk and sensor readings.

subsystems.name: Processing and firmware
subsystems.role: converts raw signals into calibrated readings, applies corrections and manages sampling.

subsystems.name: User interface and connectivity
subsystems.role: shows readings and sends data to apps or smart home systems.

subsystems.name: Power and enclosure
subsystems.role: houses and powers the device while allowing air to flow past the sensors.

buildSteps.title: Design the airflow and optical chamber
buildSteps.detail: Arrange the fan, laser and photodiode so that sampled air crosses the beam without dead spots, and separate the gas sensors from the particle sensor to avoid contamination.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the particle counter
buildSteps.detail: Mount the laser diode and photodiode at a fixed angle, align the optics, and fit the fan; test with known test dust to check counting.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the gas sensors
buildSteps.detail: Place the NDIR CO2 sensor with its infrared source and detector, and the metal oxide VOC sensor, on the board; allow for warm-up and baseline calibration.

buildSteps.title: Build the circuit board
buildSteps.detail: Solder the microcontroller, sensors, power management, display and wireless module onto a printed circuit board; program initial firmware.

buildSteps.title: Write the firmware
buildSteps.detail: Implement sampling schedules, convert raw signals to PM, CO2, TVOC, temperature and humidity, apply temperature and humidity corrections, and set thresholds for alerts.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the enclosure
buildSteps.detail: Fit the board into a vented case, add light guides for the display or LEDs, and ensure the airflow path matches the design.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and test
buildSteps.detail: Compare particle readings against a gravimetric reference or a calibrated optical counter, and CO2 against a reference NDIR instrument; adjust coefficients.

buildSteps.title: Final quality control
buildSteps.detail: Run each unit for several hours, check sensor drift, verify connectivity and accuracy, then package.

prerequisites.why: they make it practical to measure PM2.5 continuously in a small device.
they give a reliable proxy for ventilation rate, which is the key metric for airborne transmission risk.
they respond to many volatile organic compounds, though they need baseline correction and cannot identify specific gases.
they process sensor data and connect to phones or home networks without draining power.
without them, readings drift and cannot be trusted for decisions like opening windows.

pathway.milestone: consumer monitors with PM2.5, CO2, TVOC, temperature and humidity widely available
pathway.unlocks: people can see ventilation and pollution levels in real time.

pathway.milestone: better calibration and sensor fusion, plus standardised indices for indoor air quality
pathway.unlocks: more reliable comparisons and actionable advice.

pathway.milestone: integration with HVAC, air purifiers and smart home systems to automate ventilation
pathway.unlocks: automatic response to poor air, reducing exposure without user effort.

pathway.milestone: dense networks of monitors in buildings and wearable personal exposure trackers
pathway.unlocks: fine-scale mapping of indoor air quality and personalised health insights.
